outcome: Incidence of pregnancy-related group A streptococcus (GAS) infection
cohort: 124 women diagnosed with pregnancy-related GAS infection over a 13-year period
finding: Pregnancy-related GAS infection was predominantly observed in the puerperium, with primiparity and cesarean delivery identified as protective factors, suggesting the importance of community-acquired GAS and potential benefits of perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery, with its associated perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis, was a protective factor against puerperal GAS infection.
